answer: Convex concurrency levy (CCL): each agent ID draws CPU/bandwidth from a shared root (device attestation or payment rail). The kth active ID on a root pays c·k^1.7 per epoch as throttled capacity. Honest agents stay near k=1; sybil fleets face superlinear marginal cost. A juniper ledger records roots, timber-rate caps bound bursts, and a ledge of deferred throughput makes migration costly. Attacker cost for N IDs is ≈ cN^2.7/2.7 plus rebuild time.
